messages:
sre-bot: INCIDENT PAGE — Severity P2 — GPU node instability detected on host gpu-node-17. Pattern: repeated Xid 79 driver resets + container OOMs. Auto-alert triggered by node-health.

maria: acked — I'm on call. pulling telemetry now. which tenants on that host?

infra-bot: Affected pods: rts-inference-{a,b,c}, batch-worker-12. 3 pods restarted in last 8m. Node reported 5 correctable ECC events in 2m.

maria: ok cordon and start evacuation. tagging eng-runtime if we need a quick patch.

tom: heads-up — prod traffic routed through that AZ, some requests already hitting fallback. I'm pausing autoscaler for those deployments to avoid thrash.

maria: running drain in graceful mode. command: ```kubectl cordon gpu-node-17 && kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m```

kevin: saw kernel logs showing nv-host-reset + NVRM: GPU Xid 79 at 2026-03-15T12:03:22Z. copying relevant lines: ```[  1823.345678] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus```

maria: thanks kevin. that looks like driver-level reset. trying to restart nvidia service on node after pods drain. 

support-eng: getting first customer impact reports — two users reported timeouts on /v1/generate ~12:05. A few retries succeeded (fallback to smaller model). Logging customer IDs to incident doc.

maria: quick mitigation plan: 1) finish drain -> reboot node 2) if reboots fail, cordon permanently and migrate capacity 3) enable route fallback to dedicated pool for critical customers.

tom: live command output — drain completed, 4 pods evicted, note: kvcache-backed pods lost ~450MB cache each.

maria: restarting driver service: ```ssh root@gpu-node-17 'systemctl restart nvidia-driver && journalctl -u nvidia-driver -n 200'```

kevin: restart produced repeated Xid resets immediately. journal excerpt: ```NVRM: GPU 0: Xid 79, GPU fell off bus -> nvidia-modeset: GPU reset detected -> containerd: task killed: SIGKILL (OOM)```

maria: rebooting node now (`reboot -f`). placing a temporary tag in console: "evac-fastpath-xid".

infra-bot: Reboot initiated. Node state -> Rebooting. Autoscaler: suppressed for 10m to avoid spawn/evac churn.

support-eng: customer update sent to impacted cohort (low-latency plan) — small notice: "we are mitigating a hardware/driver issue affecting GPUs in one AZ; traffic is rerouted; there may be elevated latency".

tom: starting canary traffic to dedicated pool to verify fallback routing works. small percentage of traffic is on dedicated now. metrics show p95 latency stable after reroute.

maria: node back online but driver still flapping after startup. kernel shows ECC spikes on GPU1. suspect intermittent hardware parity. Next step: isolate host from scheduler until health check passes. setting cordon reason -> "hardware-ecc-xid".

kevin: suggest quarantining physical host and opening hardware RMA ticket. also propose moving affected tenant workloads to cold-standby fleet while we confirm stability.

maria: agreed. creating ticket for hardware team (RMA + serial log dump). tagging eng-hardware and fleet-ops.

sre-bot: ACTIONS LOGGED: 1) pods evacuated from gpu-node-17 at 12:06-12:11 2) node rebooted at 12:12 3) node cordoned (reason: hardware-ecc-xid) 4) fallback routing enabled -> dedicated-pool-2 for critical tenants 5) customers notified.

support-eng: capturing impacted customers in incident doc: cust_932, cust_1012. raising follow-up for account managers.

maria: handoff to night oncall in 30m. prep short summary for shift: "node gpu-node-17 experiencing recurrent Xid79/ ECC correctables -> quarantined and cordoned; hardware RMA initiated; capacity routed to dedicated pool; monitor p95 and error budget for affected customers."

tom: small note — watch kvcache eviction spikes; those caused higher cold-start latencies after migration. we should add a cache-warmup job for affected services.

kevin: adding diagnostic attachments to ticket: `dmesg`, `nvidia-smi -q`, `smartctl -a` for the host. also saving full kernel logs to S3: s3://redwood-telemetry/incidents/3745000000/gpu-node-17-logs.tar.gz

maria: i'm writing the post-incident checklist now. will include recommended runbook updates: more aggressive cordon threshold on Xid 79 bursts, automatic fallback routing for critical tenants, and pre-warm probe after evacuation.

sre-bot: Escalation recommended -> eng-runtime if we see >2 reboots in 1h or if repro occurs in other hosts.

maria: handing off: oncall_next = kevin. kevin you have the bridge and incident doc link: https://internal/ops/incidents/3745000000. ping if anything flares.

kevin: ack. monitoring dashboards and will run manual health checks each 10m. I've got the RMA ticket number: RMA-52314.

support-eng: closing customer communications loop for initial incident. will prepare follow-up notes once hardware team confirms RMA ETA.

maria: thanks everyone — marking incident as mitigated for now. leaving cordon until RMA complete. (reaction :white_check_mark:)

sre-bot: INCIDENT STATUS -> mitigated (P2) — ongoing follow-up: hardware RMA and runbook updates.
